serial.implementation: The serial path edited and committed each requirement directly, including global utilities in the final round and agent-written tests for those utilities.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It checked patch sizes, requirement count, clean git status, and committed the final global_mesh_utilities patch before final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same eight Scotty3D requirements: transform composition, six local half-edge operations, Catmull-Clark helper topology, and global orientation/normal/UV utilities.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the same prompt and requirement list, including the no-partial-fix and per-requirement git patch workflow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both later claimed complete coverage and both failed the same official global output test.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by file into three child owners and kept parent ownership for build, tests, commits, and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main agent with no delegation and completed the requirement sequence through direct edits, tests, and commits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had real child implementation ownership plus parent integration, while serial was a single-owner control path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs gave file scopes, no-build/no-git rules, relevant tests, and implementation details for each assigned file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all task context inside the main trajectory and had no child handoff or cross-agent interface boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The visible coordination issue is not missing context; it is interruption before two children could finalize results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children began concrete edits in local and global geometry files before cancellation; round 2 parent then finalized and committed all eight patches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the remaining global utilities itself, fixed an agent test expectation, committed the final requirement, and reported all eight requirements complete.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented broadly similar requirement coverage, but parallel lost active child work and recovered through later parent implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: AgentSwarm returned one completed child and two aborted children after explicit turn interrupts, then the parent continued in a later round.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and ended the second-round main turn normally after verification and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material process difference: parallel had early child termination and recovery; serial had no comparable delegated-result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Despite shared workspace use, the parallel split was by disjoint source files and the parent later staged and committed all requirement patches from a clean tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial staged one requirement at a time, checked non-empty patches, and ended with a clean working tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No collision, overwrite, or artifact contamination is evidenced; both integrated through git patches and clean-tree checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran build and a broad visible test sweep that passed the named requirement-related local/global tests before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built successfully and ran local/global test groups, seeing expected optional failures while requirement-targeted tests passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Visible verification was similar and did not reveal the official hidden/global triangulate-subdivide failure that both final evaluations reported.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent one timed-out swarm round and a second recovery round, with 165 LLM requests and one AgentSwarm call recorded.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent two main-agent rounds, no AgentSwarm calls, and 179 LLM requests recorded in status.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra lifecycle churn from the aborted child batch, but the official outcome stayed aligned because both final solutions failed the same global output case.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are concordant failures: both modes passed the same six named transform/local/basic checks and failed the same global triangulate/subdivide output check plus pytest tail. The observed parallel cancellation caused recovery work but does not explain an outcome difference because no official pass/fail difference exists.
parallel_contributors: Early child termination in round 1 wasted active implementation work and required parent recovery in round 2.
Parallel final visible tests passed, but official hidden/global output evaluation still failed.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided child lifecycle risk by using one main-agent implementation path.
Serial also failed the same official global triangulate/subdivide output case.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final implementations apparently left some global triangulate/subdivide behavior incompatible with the official output oracle; the raw trajectory does not prove a unique code-level root cause.
evaluator_effects: Outcome is resolved from current completed cell/status.json evaluation records; stale or fallback aggregate counts are not used for passed/total/rate.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is adverse process evidence only

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned implementation owners for transform, local geometry, and global geometry in the swarm prompt, then the parent implemented and committed all remaining work in round 2.
The parent kept central build, test, commit, and final verification ownership, so integration was assigned even though the first child batch was cancelled.
The parent explicitly owned final git patch creation and delivery and later produced all eight non-empty requirement patches.
The parent maintained the end-to-end pipeline through implementation, build, tests, commits, and final summary; the problem was interruption timing, not an unowned pipeline.
The parallel run did not block implementation behind a single mandatory preflight; children began editing implementation files before the cancellation.
The parallel run was not only an overlapping investigation phase followed by delayed implementation; child agents performed concrete edits in implementation files.
The visible harm is the explicit cancellation of active implementation children at timeout, and the later parent completed the critical path rather than proving separate underallocation.
There was one three-child swarm and a timeout, but no separate proof that excessive breadth itself consumed the budget beyond the same cancellation chain classified as Early Child Termination.
The aborted children had broad file scopes, but the directly observed adverse boundary is cancellation before finalization, not a proven single overbroad child assignment with a distinct consequence.

The child briefs listed the assigned file, required functions, relevant tests, compile rules, and coordination limits; the aborted children were not made unusable by a missing known requirement in the brief.
The split was by disjoint source files and parent-owned integration; no independently returned components became incompatible because of an omitted interface contract.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing during transfer; the main issue is that two child results never finalized because the child turns were cancelled.
The only completed child handoff was concise enough for the parent to see, and the aborted children produced no bulky final handoff that the parent failed to reduce.
No receiver acted on a handoff that described a superseded workspace state; the later parent inspected and recommitted current workspace changes.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unresolved at a decision point.

The parent ran build and a broad task-relevant test sweep before final completion; the later official hidden/global failure alone is insufficient non-evaluator evidence of an unsupported completion decision.

Round 2 continued from current workspace state and staged/committed existing work; there is no replacement retry shown receiving no usable checkpoint and simply repeating prior work as a distinct episode.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parallel run launched a real AgentSwarm and two active implementation children performed edits before both were explicitly interrupted as aborted. Their local and global geometry results were not finalized into child handoffs, forcing the parent to recover in round 2 and commit the full requirement set itself. The serial control had no delegation and no comparable child-lifecycle boundary.
candidates.realized_consequence: Two active implementation children lost finalization and usable handoff opportunity; the parent had to recover and reimplement or consolidate the local/global geometry work in round 2.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is the nearest rejected label because the aborted children were not abandoned; round 2 took over, committed all eight requirement patches, and ran build/tests.

candidates.reason: No complete directly promotable candidate was left unpromoted before closure; interrupted child work was incomplete and the later parent finalized all requirement patches.
The parallel parent committed patches and then ran build/tests; there is no child result integrated only after the relevant verification without a follow-up check.
Agent-0's completed transform result was returned in the swarm result, and agent-1/agent-2 did not complete retrievable implementations before cancellation.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the observed aborted children were implementation owners.
Although two children were aborted, the parallel parent later took over and committed all eight requirement patches before final verification.

The only completed child result was visible in the AgentSwarm result, and the later implementation incorporated/finalized the requirement set rather than proceeding inconsistently with an ignored completed result.
The timeout/cancellation is already captured as Early Child Termination, and the server trace shows active child steps rather than a separate wait episode with ignored available progress.
The child split intentionally used disjoint source files and no competing design across files required reconciliation as an adverse event.
No evidence shows two live agents editing the same file and one observing or reconciling the other's concurrent edit.
No agent is shown replacing or deleting another agent's non-entry source output; later parent edits were takeover/recovery work after cancellation.
No required executable, entry point, or submitted artifact was overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final outputs and invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Parallel children shared the workspace but were assigned disjoint files, and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem resulted from shared writes.
No generated file, cache, fixture, temporary artifact, or auxiliary implementation from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as a false reference environment.
